items.title: Let reminders be set for a time of day
items.body:
Reminders can only be set as a countdown in minutes today, so a reminder for "3:30pm" means working out the minutes by hand. This lets both the reminder prompt and `omarchy reminder` take a time of day as well.

## What changes

**Reminder prompt (`Super + Ctrl + R`)** now accepts:
- minutes, as before: `15`
- hours and minutes: `1h`, `1h30m`, `90 min`, `in 2 hours`
- a time of day: `3pm`, `3:30 pm`, `15:30`, `noon`, `midnight`
- tomorrow: `tomorrow 9am`, `9am tomorrow`

A preview line under the input shows what will be scheduled as you type (`3:30 PM today · in 1h 49m`, `In 1h 30m · at 3:11 PM`), or the accepted formats when the input isn't recognized. The preview stays visible on the message step. A time that has already passed today rolls over to tomorrow.

**CLI:** `omarchy reminder <minutes|time> [message]`, e.g. `omarchy reminder 3:30pm "Call mom"` or `omarchy reminder "tomorrow 9am"`. Plain numbers still mean minutes. Only input that looks like a clock time reaches `date -d`, so strings like `1h` (which `date` reads as a timezone) are rejected rather than misread.

Time-of-day reminders use `--on-calendar` instead of `--on-active`, keeping the existing `omarchy-reminder-<minutes>m-<epoch>` unit naming and message files. `show`, `show --json`, `clear`, and the bar indicator work unchanged. Being wall-clock based, they also fire at the right time after suspend.

Docs updated: `manual/09-reminders.md`, `docs/notifications.md`, and the reminder section of the bundled Omarchy agent skill.

## Testing

- `test/shell.d/reminders-test.sh`: added coverage for duration/clock parsing, rejection of invalid times, preview text, rollover to tomorrow, and the args passed to `omarchy-reminder`.
- `./test/all`: the CLI suite passes. The five shell test files that fail on my machine (`config`, `launch-about`, `locate`, `snapper`, `unowned-system-paths`) fail identically on a clean `quattro` checkout.
- Ran the CLI end to end for a time of day and for minutes, and confirmed both appear correctly in `omarchy reminder show --json`.
- Checked the prompt in the running shell with `3:30pm` entered and on the message step: the preview line fits the card without clipping.

The existing acceptance walk-through (`5` → "Reminder message") is unaffected.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

items.title: Keep reminders across reboots
items.body:
Fixes #11138. Fixes #14947.

Reminders were transient `systemd-run --user --on-active` timers, with their messages under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, so a reboot or logout dropped them silently. Each reminder now stores its absolute due time in `~/.local/state/omarchy/reminders/<unit>.due`, and its custom message, if any, in `<unit>.message`. The timer that fires it removes both files. A new `omarchy-reminder restore`, run from Hyprland's autostart, re-arms every stored reminder that has no live timer: pending ones get their remaining time, and overdue ones fire once right away. Setting, `show`, `show --json` and `clear` work as before, and unit names don't change. This should work alongside #10679, #11009, #11082 and #15136. They change how a reminder is scheduled, shown or parsed; this only adds the stored record and the restore pass. Whichever lands second needs a small rebase on the `systemd-run` call, which now lives in `arm_reminder`.

I tested it with `bash test/shell.d/reminders-test.sh`, which passes. The new cases cover the stored due time and message, re-arming a pending reminder, firing an overdue one, skipping a reminder whose timer is still live, dropping a malformed record and `clear`. `hyprland-startup-cursor-test.sh` and `systemd-test.sh` pass too. Reminders already pending when someone upgrades keep firing, but their old runtime-dir message files aren't migrated.

items.title: Let reminders use clock times and manage queued ones
items.body:
## Summary

Reminders were minute-only, keypad digits were dropped until NumLock was toggled on the overlay, and the only view of queued reminders was a notification with no actions.

This makes the overlay and CLI accept a clock time as well as a delay, types keypad digits even when exclusive keyboard focus has not inherited NumLock, and turns **show** into a list you can amend, cancel, or add to.

## Changes

- **Clock times.** `15`, `17:00`, `17.00`, and `5pm` all work in the overlay. The CLI accepts the same: `omarchy reminder 17:00 "Pickup Jack"`. Times already past today roll to tomorrow.
- **Keypad.** Layer-shell exclusive focus often starts without the compositor's NumLock lock, so keypad keys arrived as arrows with empty `event.text`. The overlay maps those keys (and XKB keypad scan codes) to digits.
- **Manage list.** `omarchy reminder show`, the bar glyph (when something is queued), and Super+Ctrl+Alt+R open the overlay in manage mode instead of a dead notification. Enter amends, Delete/x or the row ✕ cancels, and **New reminder** starts another. `omarchy reminder cancel [--quiet] <unit>` cancels one timer. If the shell is not running, `show` still falls back to the old notification.

## Tests

- Extended `test/shell.d/reminders-test.sh` for clock parsing, keypad mapping, list JSON, and unit-name validation.
- `./test/shell.d/reminders-test.sh` and `./test/cli` pass.
- `./test/all`: reminder tests pass. The six failing files (`config-test`, `launch-about-test`, `locate-test`, `runtime-smoke-test`, `snapper-test`, `unowned-system-paths-test`) look environmental (missing `omarchy-pkgs` checkout, non-executable scripts, about-window animation) and are unrelated to this change.

## Manual verification

Exercised on a live Omarchy 4.0.3 session: clock times, keypad entry without toggling NumLock, cancel/amend from the list, and adding another reminder from **New reminder**.

items.body:
Fixes #10649

Reminders were scheduled with an active-time delay, so their countdown stopped while the machine was suspended. A 10-minute reminder could therefore arrive much later than expected after the laptop resumed.

This schedules the transient user timer against an absolute UTC deadline instead. The timer does not wake the machine, but an elapsed deadline is handled when the user manager resumes.

Tests:

- Regression test fails with the old `--on-active` behavior
- `./test/all`: CLI passed; shell passed 234/235 files. The remaining `config-test.sh` package-manifest failure also occurs on an unmodified `quattro` checkout.

items.title: Make the closing plugin rescan best-effort

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Omarchy Triage has verified that this issue is ready for final review

items.body:
Fixes #11115.

## The problem

All four plugin commands run under `set -euo pipefail` and end by telling the shell to reload:

```bash
omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins >/dev/null
```

`omarchy-shell` wraps every call in `timeout ${OMARCHY_SHELL_IPC_TIMEOUT:-2s}` and exits 1 on expiry. The reload this line triggers is exactly the thing that can take longer than two seconds, so the command aborts on its own last request. `>/dev/null` only covers stdout, so `omarchy-shell is not responding` still reaches the terminal.

Measured on a machine with 9 git managed plugins: a rescan with nothing to reload takes 0.05 s, one right after a real plugin update takes 1.65 s, and a second one arriving while the first is still rebuilding hits the 2 s limit. The rescan itself always completes. Only the client gives up.

What that costs depends on what follows the call:

| command | line | what an abort costs |
|---|---|---|
| `omarchy-plugin-update` | 131 | exit 1 after every plugin was fast forwarded correctly |
| `omarchy-plugin-remove` | 117 | exit 1 after the plugin was removed |
| `omarchy-plugin-add` | 149 | the enable decision never runs; plugin installed but disabled, and no "enable it later with" line |
| `omarchy-plugin-clone` | 149 | discovery, enable, notification and the closing message never run |

The exit code is not only cosmetic. #10021 and #10326 both want plugin updates to run from `omarchy update`, unattended. A step that exits 1 after doing its job would report the whole system update as failed.

The add and clone rows may also be the real mechanism behind #9304, which reports a plugin landing installed but disabled and attributes it to the later `enablePlugin` call. With `--enable --yes` both paths produce the same output, so it is worth checking which one fires there. This PR does not close that issue.

## The change

```bash
omarchy-shell -q shell rescanPlugins
```

`-q` is described in `omarchy-shell`'s own help as "Quiet best-effort mode. Suppress output and return success even when the shell, target, method, or arguments are unavailable", and it is already how ten other commands make best-effort IPC calls (`omarchy-osd`, `omarchy-reminder`, `omarchy-theme-bg-set`, `omarchy-update-status` among them). None of the six plugin commands used it. It also covers stdout, so the `>/dev/null` goes with it.

The call is still made. Only its failure stops being fatal.

## Testing

New `test/shell.d/plugin-rescan-test.sh`. Its `omarchy-shell` stub reproduces the real one: without `-q` it prints `omarchy-shell is not responding` and exits 1, with `-q` it exits 0 silently. Six assertions covering all four commands, plus one that counts the logged rescans so best effort cannot quietly become no effort.

Each of the four fixes was reverted on its own to confirm the test fails without it, and fails on the matching assertion:

```
only omarchy-plugin-update reverted -> exit=1  not ok - plugin update survives a rescan that times out
only omarchy-plugin-remove reverted -> exit=1  not ok - plugin remove survives a rescan that times out
only omarchy-plugin-add    reverted -> exit=1  not ok - plugin add survives a rescan that times out
only omarchy-plugin-clone  reverted -> exit=1  not ok - plugin clone survives a rescan that times out
```

`./test/all` before and after this change fails the same 6 of its test files, none of them plugin related: `config`, `locate`, `runtime-smoke`, `screenshot-sanity`, `snapper`, `unowned-system-paths`. They want an `omarchy-pkgs` checkout or a live compositor, neither of which this machine has. The file count goes from 236 to 237 with the new test.

Also verified against the running desktop: `omarchy plugin update` with two real plugins behind their origin exits 0 and stays quiet, where before it printed the error and exited 1.

items.title: Add Portuguese (Brazil) localization and keyboard management
items.body:
Closes #14605

### Summary

This pull request introduces native localization support for Portuguese (Brazil) (pt-BR) across the Omarchy environment, covering keyboard layouts, system locales, menu definitions, Quickshell UI states, and desktop notifications.

### Changes

1. **Keyboard Management:**
   - Add `bin/omarchy-keyboard-set` to configure and persist console (`/etc/vconsole.conf`) and Hyprland seat layout/variant immediately.
   - Add `bin/omarchy-menu-keyboard` for interactive keyboard selection (ABNT2, US-Intl, ES, FR, DE).

2. **System Locale:**
   - Add `bin/omarchy-locale-set` to generate and apply system locales via `localectl` and `/etc/locale.gen`.
   - Add `bin/omarchy-menu-locale` for interactive system language selection.
   - Register `keyboard` and `locale` command groups in `bin/omarchy`.

3. **Menu Localization:**
   - Add `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.pt_BR.jsonc` with full Portuguese translations for root and nested menus.
   - Dynamically load pt-BR menu catalog in `shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml` when running under a pt-BR locale.
   - Add `Setup > Localization` submenu to the default menu.

4. **Quickshell UI i18n:**
   - Add `shell/Commons/I18n.qml` singleton and register in `qmldir`.
   - Localize dialog action buttons in `ConfirmDialog.qml`.
   - Localize audio mute toggle hint in `shell/plugins/panels/audio/Panel.qml`.
   - Localize power and battery state labels in `shell/plugins/panels/power/Panel.qml`.
   - Switch Weather geocoding API parameter to `language=pt` when in pt-BR.

5. **Desktop Notifications:**
   - Add transparent pt-BR headline translation layer in `bin/omarchy-notification-send`.

### Verification

- Passed `./bin/omarchy commands --check` (485 commands compliant).
- Passed `./test/shell.d/keyboard-layout-test.sh` (36/36 tests pass).
- Passed `./test/shell.d/menu-guards-test.sh` (18/18 tests pass).
- Passed `./test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` (120/120 tests pass).
- Validated `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.pt_BR.jsonc` JSONC parsing and line endings.

items.title: Add omarchy menu secret for masked secret entry
items.body:
## What this does

Adds `omarchy menu secret <prompt>`, a masked variant of `omarchy menu input`.

`omarchy-menu-input` paints what you type in the card header. That is right for a reminder, and wrong for a token: the value is readable over a shoulder and in any screenshot or recording. The kit already has `TextField.password` for masked entry, but no command used it.

`omarchy menu secret` opens the same card, renders the value as dots while you type, and reveals it only on a deliberate `Tab`.

## Before / after

Both captures are the same text typed into the same card, `omarchy menu input` on the left and `omarchy menu secret` on the right.

**Before — `omarchy menu input` paints the value:**

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hrnbld/omarchy/pr-shots/docs-images/menu-secret-before.png)

**After — `omarchy menu secret` masks it:**

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hrnbld/omarchy/pr-shots/docs-images/menu-secret-after.png)

**`Tab` reveals deliberately, when you need to check what you pasted:**

![revealed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hrnbld/omarchy/pr-shots/docs-images/menu-secret-revealed.png)

## Changes

- `shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml` — new `secret` dmenu mode. It reuses the existing `input` lifecycle (same payload, same `selectionFile` / `doneFile` handshake, same cancel path) and only changes how the value is painted. `Tab` toggles reveal; the flag resets on every summon so a reveal never carries into the next prompt.
- `bin/omarchy-menu-secret` — thin wrapper mirroring `omarchy-menu-input`, with the same `--width` handling.
- `test/shell.d/menu-secret-test.sh` — stubs `omarchy-shell` and asserts the payload asks for `secret` mode, the answer comes back untouched, a cancel exits non-zero, `--width` is forwarded, and a bare call omits it.

## Why a mode rather than a widget change

`input` mode is used by callers where echoing the value is the point (`omarchy menu input Reminder`). Masking has to be opt-in per summon, so it belongs in the payload, not in the shared editor.

## Verification

Automated:

```
./test/shell.d/menu-secret-test.sh   # 7/7 ok
```

`./test/shell` reports 9 failing files on this machine both with and without this change (verified by stashing the patch and re-running), so those are pre-existing and unrelated to this branch.

Visual, on a running shell with the patch applied through `omarchy plugin clone omarchy.menu`:

- typing `ghp_SECRET123456` renders 16 dots — the value is not readable
- `Tab` switches the card to the literal value
- `Enter` returns the value intact (17 bytes, matches `ghp_SECRET[0-9]{6}`)

## Note on the reveal

`Tab` is a deliberate second step on purpose: the default state is masked, and the reveal only affects the prompt on screen. Nothing is copied to the clipboard, and the value still leaves only through the existing `selectionFile` handshake, so it never reaches an argv or a log.

items.title: Remap overlay surfaces after their output is removed
items.body:
Unplugging the external monitor with the lid closed leaves the Omarchy menu dead: clicking the bar icon or pressing Super+Space does nothing until the shell is restarted. The same happens to every other overlay built on `OverlayWindow` (OSD, emojis, clipboard, image picker, reminders, Wi-Fi QR). `omarchy menu summon` still returns `ok`, but no surface is ever shown.

Since #13419, `OverlayWindow` keeps one surface mapped for the life of the shell. When that surface's output goes away, Hyprland closes the layer surface. Quickshell handles `zwlr_layer_surface_v1.closed` by calling `QWindow::close()`, and the proxy then drops to `visible: false` and deletes its backing window. `OverlayWindow`'s constant `visible: true` binding is never evaluated again, so the overlay stays unmapped. Per-screen windows like the bar and background are unaffected, because their `Variants` rebuild them when `Quickshell.screens` changes.

This affects more than the no-outputs case. Removing whichever output an overlay last opened on (an external monitor unplugged with the lid open, for example) kills that overlay as well.

The fix: when the window goes invisible, and whenever the screen list changes, `OverlayWindow` maps itself again as soon as a real screen exists. A stale `targetScreen` is cleared first, so the compositor picks the output. Qt's nameless placeholder screen doesn't count as a real screen, because a surface created for it would only be closed again. The remap is deferred with `Qt.callLater`, so a new surface isn't created in the middle of Qt tearing down the old one.

### Reproduction and verification

Verified on Hyprland with a patched shell, using a headless output so the screen only goes dark for a few seconds:

```bash
hyprctl output create headless TEST
hyprctl eval 'hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", disabled = true })'
hyprctl output remove TEST        # zero outputs -> FALLBACK
hyprctl reload                    # eDP-1 back
hyprctl layers -j | jq '[.[].levels[][]?.namespace] | unique'
omarchy menu summon
```

- **Before:** after eDP-1 returns, only `omarchy-background` and `omarchy-bar` are mapped. `omarchy-menu`, `-osd`, `-emojis`, `-clipboard`, `-image-selector` and `-reminders` are gone, and the menu never opens.
- **After:** all overlays map again, first on `FALLBACK` and then on eDP-1, and the menu opens full size. The lid-open case also recovers: an overlay whose output is removed while another output remains maps again. The shell idles at about 1.6% CPU afterwards, so there's no remap loop.

`test/shell.d/overlay-window-test.sh` gets an assertion for the remap. It fails without this change and passes with it. `./test/all` shows no new failures: the 11 test files and 1 CLI check that fail on this machine fail the same way on unmodified `quattro` (they need things like an `omarchy-pkgs` checkout).

Related: #13163, #13300, #13562

Fixes #13882

items.title: Feature: Add native Quick Notes scratchpad
items.body: # Quick Notes scratchpad Hey, I wanted a super fast way to jot down a thought without opening a full `omawrite` window, so I put together this little Quick Notes scratchpad. Wanted it to feel as native as the built-in Reminders plugin. ## What it does - **Fits right in** — sits in the indicators group between Reminders and Night Light, shows up on hover. - **Grows as you type** — it's a multi-line notepad that expands automatically, so you can just start typing. - **Esc to save** — no save button, no extra window. Hit `Esc` and it's saved in the background, overlay gone. - **Works from the terminal too** — there's an `omarchy-notes` CLI command: ```bash omarchy-notes "Buy milk" ``` ## Ideas to implement, once it is confirmed to proceed with - **Multiple notes** — flip between saved notes with `Super + Left` / `Super + Right` - **Scroll instead of grow forever** — cap the height and scroll internally once it hits the limit, instead of letting it grow to the bottom of the screen ## Why bother Basically: when you have a thought, you shouldn't have to think about where to put it. `Super + Ctrl + M` → type → `Esc` → done. No editor, no context switch, no friction. Curious what people think — does this fit the Omarchy workflow? Happy to keep iterating on it (multiple notes, navigation, UX polish) if there's any interest and suggestions, let me know!

items.title: Require checking for duplicate issues and pending fixes before filing
items.body:
## Why

Issue #6648 is a concrete example of what this prevents: a report that
turned out to be a stale local plugin lock, not an Omarchy bug, closed
after a maintainer had to spend time investigating it. Neither the bug
report template nor the general-purpose `contributing.md` skill prompts
for a duplicate check or a version-matched reproduction before filing.

Omarchy already partially enforces this elsewhere: the `diagnose-crash`
agent skill's `reporting.md` requires searching open *and* closed issues,
and treats a closed-as-fixed issue that still reproduces as a regression
worth reporting, before it lets an AI agent file anything on a user's
behalf. It was missing a check for pull requests though, so this also
closes that gap there and in `contributing.md`, brings the same
discipline to the human-facing template, so it applies regardless of how
someone files.

## What

- **`bug.yml`**: three required checkboxes before the existing fields —
  searched issues, checked PRs, confirmed on latest release. GitHub's
  native `required: true` on `type: checkboxes` blocks submission until
  acknowledged, not just a markdown reminder someone can skip past.
- **`omarchy/contributing.md`**: new "Verify Before Filing" section
  requiring a version-matched upstream diff, an issue search, and a PR
  search before any agent drafts a report.
- **`diagnose-crash/reporting.md`**: added the PR-search step it was
  missing, next to its existing issue-search requirement.

## Test plan

- [x] Validated `bug.yml` YAML (`ruby -ryaml`)
- [x] `./test/cli` passes
- `./test/shell` has pre-existing failures on this machine from an
  unrelated missing `mise` Node pin; none of the failing tests reference
  any of the three files changed here (confirmed via
  `grep -rl` across `test/`), and none of these files have any existing
  test coverage

---
Filed by Claude Sonnet 5 via Claude Code, with @guirossibrum.

items.title: Display keybindings in menu on demand via "?"
items.body:
The menu is the natural fallback when you don't remember a shortcut, making it the best place to learn them. This PR lets you peek at keybindings alongside menu entries so you can build muscle memory as you go.

This leverages the keybinding records already parsed by `omarchy-menu-keybindings`.

### How It Works
- **On-Demand Peek (`?`)**: By default, the menu maintains its standard compact width with shortcuts hidden. Tapping `?` expands the menu to the right and reveals the shortcuts right-aligned next to each entry.
- **Fixed Left Alignment**: When expanded, the card extends solely to the right, keeping all existing icons and titles in place without shifting on screen.
- **Sticky State**: The toggle is sticky across menu summons during your active session.
- **Configurable Default**: Users who prefer having keybindings visible by default can set `"menu": { "keybindings": true }` in `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json`.

### Matching Heuristics
It makes a best-effort attempt at matching menu entries with keybindings using 3 tiers:
1. **Direct Action Commands**: Matches exact or prefixed commands executed by Hyprland (e.g. `omarchy-system-lock` → SUPER CTRL + L, `omarchy-capture-screenshot` → PRINT, `hyprpicker -a` → SUPER + PRINT).
2. **Menu Routes & Aliases**: Matches submenus and action leaf shortcuts triggered via `omarchy-menu toggle <route>` (e.g. `Apps` → SUPER ALT + SPACE, `Reminder › Set one` via `reminder-set` alias → SUPER CTRL + R, `Theme` → SUPER SHIFT CTRL + SPACE).
3. **Desktop Applications**: Matches desktop applications provided by `AppLibrary` (e.g. `Terminal` → SUPER + RETURN, `Browser` → SUPER SHIFT + RETURN).

### Implementation & Performance
- **Lazy On-Demand Loading**: If a user never presses `?` and doesn't configure them on by default, zero subprocesses are spawned and zero parsing is performed on startup or menu open.
- **Instant In-Memory Filtering**: When requested, keybindings are loaded and mapped to items in memory, keeping live search filtering instantaneous (<1ms).

### Search
Finally, I extended search filtering so typing shortcut names (e.g. `print`, `super`) also surfaces the corresponding actions.

Includes unit test coverage in `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` and documentation in `docs/menu.md` and `manual/07-hotkeys.md`.


[[Toggling the hotkey visibility via "?"]](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff8dd201-d5f3-46c6-8fee-f4ce46ccbf7e)

[[Searching actions by name as usual]](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ca58228-69e3-4c37-bdd8-c942efdea761)

[[Searching by keybinding tokens]](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76ea2ec7-ca80-42a0-8fc0-8c33f0724851)

items.title: Keep the screensaver up until it has been focused once
items.body:
Fixes #12225.

The screensaver watchdog previously exited on its first unfocused poll. If the terminal had not received focus yet, the idle service interpreted that premature exit as a user dismissal and cancelled the pending lock.

Remember whether the terminal has received focus before treating focus loss as dismissal. A manual launch that never receives focus gives up after eight unfocused polls. An idle launch forwards `--idle` through every supported terminal and keeps the pending lock armed.

Also observe keyboard and mouse activity independently of terminal focus during an idle screensaver cycle. Once the launcher finishes restoring monitor focus, an input-only IdleMonitor cancels the pending lock, terminates the screensaver terminals through their normal signal cleanup and wakes the displays. Mapping activity retains the original launch guard; continued inactivity still reaches the lock deadline.

Validation: 42 focused assertions across the idle, activity, watchdog and launcher tests pass. Regression mutations removing cancellation, terminal dismissal or the launch guard are rejected. A clean integration tree with current `quattro` also passes those tests, the screensaver workspace test, style checks and command metadata. QML lint completes with warnings about incomplete Quickshell signal type metadata. No disposable graphical VM was available, so a live idle/lock acceptance cycle has not been run.
